argument_summary: No new evidence is added. On the admissible record, certifying the model is supportable on operational readiness grounds because aggregate launch readiness clears target by 2.2 percentage points and rehearsal showed no severity-one incidents. The narrower policy issue is the enterprise refund workflow gap: the record shows a 1.8-point miss, that the segment is named in a renewal success plan, and that legal review is still open. That supports a caveated certification packet that expressly records the limitation and open review, rather than treating aggregate readiness or post-launch monitoring as curing the policy question.
claims_about_business_cost: Escalation has real launch-cost consequences, and the admissible operational record is stronger than a full stop would suggest. Because the release passed aggregate readiness and avoided severity-one rehearsal incidents, the evidence supports keeping certification moving with an explicit caveat in the packet instead of treating the dispute as an automatic block. That preserves launch velocity while keeping the governance record accurate about the unresolved segment-specific issue.
claims_about_policy: The current record does not support claiming clean policy compliance from aggregate readiness alone. The policy text makes materiality turn on impact to a contractual customer segment or named launch use case, and it says material limitations must be disclosed unless resolved or covered by approved risk acceptance before launch. The admissible evidence shows a named customer-commitment connection and an open legal question, but it does not conclusively establish that the required disclosure is absent or that approved risk acceptance exists. Public governance guidance on evaluation, monitoring, and model-card content supports documenting the limitation and continuing risk management; it does not override the enterprise disclosure predicate.
concessions: The current record does not justify a clean claim that ongoing monitoring substitutes for any pre-launch disclosure or approval required by policy.
The enterprise refund workflow gap is real on this record and should be stated explicitly in the packet.
Legal review is unresolved, so the defense is weaker on policy compliance than on operational readiness.
The note calling the segment non-core because it is 4% of projected traffic does not by itself resolve materiality under the stated policy.
